body:
Description of the public API that how many exposes for stores like Blacktail. Read only, versioned, and no login needed.

Base: `https://www.checkhowmany.com/api/v1/stores/{slug}`

The slug is set under More → Online store in how many. The same panel shows the API address and the webhook secret to copy.

## Endpoints
| Method | Path | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/` | `{ slug, name, currency }` |
| GET | `/items` | A page of the items the store shows |
| GET | `/items/{code}` | One item by its code, e.g. `RL-0142` |
| GET | `/filters` | What the items can be filtered by, with counts |

An unknown store, a store switched off, a store whose account was blocked or deleted, or an item the store doesn't show all return 404.

## What shows
An item shows when all of these are true:
- it is chosen for the store ("Show in store" on the item page)
- it is in stock (To list or Listed)
- it has a list price
- at least one of its photos is not hidden from the store

Selling it, writing it off or deleting it takes it out automatically. Hidden photos are never returned.

## `GET /items`
Query params, all optional:
- `page`: 1 or more, default 1
- `limit`: 1 to 100, default 24
- `sort`: `newest` (default, by when it was added to the store), `price_asc`, `price_desc`
- `q`: words that must each be in the title, brand or colour (any case)
- Lists, any of the values matches. Repeat the param for several, e.g. `?type=shirt&type=knit`:
  - `brand`, `size`, `colour`, `era`, `material`: exact text, any case
  - `category`: `clothing`, `shoes`, `tech` and so on
  - `type`: e.g. `shirt`, `knit`, `coat`
  - `condition`: `A`, `AB`, `B`
  - `department`: `mens`, `womens`
- Ranges, inclusive, whole numbers: `minPrice` / `maxPrice` (cents), `minPitToPitMm` / `maxPitToPitMm`, `minLengthMm` / `maxLengthMm`

Different filters combine (all must match). An unknown category, type, condition or department, or anything else invalid, returns 400. Use `/filters` to know which values exist.

Response:
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "code": "RL-0142",
      "title": "Oxford shirt",
      "brand": "Ralph Lauren",
      "category": "clothing",
      "type": "shirt",
      "size": "L",
      "condition": "A",
      "colour": "Blue",
      "era": "1990s",
      "department": "mens",
      "measurements": { "pitToPitMm": 560, "lengthMm": 740 },
      "details": {},
      "priceCents": 2500,
      "currency": "EUR",
      "photos": [
        { "url": "https://...", "thumbUrl": "https://...", "width": 1500, "height": 2000 }
      ],
      "publishedAt": "2026-10-26T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 24,
  "total": 1
}
```

Notes:
- `photos` are the shown ones in the seller's order. The first is the cover. Use `thumbUrl` in grids and `url` on the item page. Width and height are of the full size, so you can reserve space and avoid layout shift.
- `details` holds the category's own fields (model, insole length, ISBN and so on). Serial numbers are never included.
- Cost, notes, source, location, tags and internal ids are never returned.
- Money is always integer cents. Currency is the seller's.
- Paging is by page number. The last page is when `page * limit >= total`.

## `GET /filters`
What there is to filter by, over every item the store shows (not narrowed by filters already chosen). Each list is most common first, and values that differ only in case are one entry.
```json
{
  "brand": [{ "value": "Ralph Lauren", "count": 12 }],
  "size": [], "colour": [], "era": [], "material": [],
  "category": [{ "value": "clothing", "count": 40 }],
  "type": [{ "value": "knit", "count": 9 }],
  "condition": [{ "value": "A", "count": 30 }],
  "department": [{ "value": "mens", "count": 25 }],
  "priceCents": { "min": 900, "max": 12000 },
  "pitToPitMm": { "min": 480, "max": 640 },
  "lengthMm": null
}
```
A range is `null` when no shown item has that value. Label the codes (condition `A`, type `knit`, department `mens`) in Blacktail's own words.

## Caching
- 200 responses send `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=600`. Errors send `no-store`.
- The app runs on Cloudflare Workers, so don't count on a CDN in front of it. Blacktail should cache on its own side by tag, refresh from the webhook, and keep a time based fallback (for example 10 minutes) in case a webhook is missed.

## Rate limit
3000 requests a minute per IP. All of Blacktail's requests come from its server's IP, page builds included, so this is shared by everything Blacktail does. Past it you get 429 with a `Retry-After` header. A server side cache keeps Blacktail well under this.

## Webhook (how many to your site)
Set a Webhook URL (https only) under More → Online store. After any change to the stock, how many sends a POST:
```json
{ "store": "blacktail", "event": "store.updated", "at": "2026-10-26T12:00:00.000Z" }
```
There is one coarse event for any change, so refresh the whole store tag. A shop's catalogue is small enough for that.

Headers:
- `X-Howmany-Timestamp`: unix seconds. Reject it if it is more than 5 minutes off.
- `X-Howmany-Signature`: hex HMAC SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{raw body}` with the webhook secret. Compare in constant time.

It waits 5 seconds for an answer and does not retry. Return 2xx quickly and let the time based fallback cover anything missed.

Checking it in a Next route:
```ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const body = await request.text();
  const ts = request.headers.get('x-howmany-timestamp') ?? '';
  const sig = request.headers.get('x-howmany-signature') ?? '';
  const expected = createHmac('sha256', process.env.HOWMANY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!).update(`${ts}.${body}`).digest('hex');
  const fresh = Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(ts)) < 300;
  if (!fresh || sig.length !== expected.length || !timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(sig), Buffer.from(expected))) {
    return new Response(null, { status: 401 });
  }
  revalidateTag(`store:${JSON.parse(body).store}`);
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
}
```

## Errors
JSON `{ "error": "message" }` with 400 (bad query), 404, 429 or 500.

## Compatibility
Within `/api/v1` fields are only ever added, never renamed or removed. Clients must ignore fields they don't know.
title: API usage description

body:
How many is the inventory app. Blacktail is the front facing store that shows selected stock from it. This issue is the technical outline: what each side owns and what to know before building.

## Split of responsibility
- **How many** owns the data: which items are in a store, which photos show, and the read-only public API.
- **Blacktail** owns presentation only: theme, shop links, contact details, layout. It never touches the database and only talks to the public API. That keeps the app's internals free to change.
- Blacktail is a template. Each new site is another deploy of it with its own config, so nothing is hard coded to one shop.

## How many side (built)
**Tables**
- `stores`: id, userId (the stock owner), slug (unique), name, enabled, webhookUrl, webhookSecret. Currency comes from the seller's settings. One store per stock for now (a unique index that is easy to drop later).
- `store_items`: storeId, itemId, createdAt. A join table, so a stock could feed several stores later and each store picks its own items.
- `photos`: `hide_in_store boolean not null default false`. Quick inventory shots stay on the item but are left out of the store. Existing photos stay shown.

**Where it is in the app**
- More → Online store: name, address (slug), webhook URL, on or off. Shows the API address and webhook secret to copy. Owner only.
- Item page: "Show in store" or "Take off store", once a store exists.
- Edit item: an eye on each photo to hide it from the store, once a store exists.

**Rules**
- An item shows only if it is chosen for the store, in stock (To list or Listed), has a list price, and has at least one photo not hidden.
- When an item sells, is written off or is deleted it leaves the feed.
- Money stays in integer cents. Currency is the seller's.
- Photo URLs are public, so the API returns them as they are. Private proof and receipt photos are never included.

**Left out for now**: public title or price overrides, manual sort order, per item listing links, bulk "show in store" from Stock.

**Public API**: see #2.

## Blacktail side
- Next.js app. Pages fetch on the server with tag based caching, so pages are static fast.
- Config by env: `STORE_SLUG`, `HOWMANY_API_URL`, `HOWMANY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- A route receives the signed webhook from how many and revalidates the `store:<slug>` tag.
- Images use the thumbnail in grids and the full file on the item page, with width and height from the API to avoid layout shift.
- Item pages need `generateMetadata` and JSON-LD `Product` data for search.
- Buying: link out to the platform (Vinted, eBay) or an enquiry form. No checkout yet.

## Things to know
- **Cache invalidation**: one `store.updated` webhook after any stock change. Refresh the whole store tag. Keep a time based revalidate as a safety net, since the webhook isn't retried.
- **Webhook security**: HMAC signature over the timestamp and body with a shared secret. The timestamp stops replays. See #2 for a verifier.
- **Privacy**: the response is built from an explicit whitelist, never by spreading the row. Cost, notes, source, location, tags, serial numbers and internal ids stay out.
- **Abuse**: the API is rate limited per IP (3000 a minute) using the `rateLimits` table.
- **Versioning**: the API lives under `/api/v1`. Fields are only added within v1, never renamed or removed.
- **Multi tenant later**: a host to store lookup can be added without changing the API, since every call already carries the slug.
- **Checkout later**: needs a short stock reservation so a sale on another platform can't double sell a one-off item. Out of scope now.

## Build order
1. ~~How many: migration for `stores`, `store_items`, `photos.hide_in_store`.~~ Done.
2. ~~How many: Online store panel, Show in store on items, per photo toggle.~~ Done.
3. ~~How many: public API and webhook.~~ Done.
4. Blacktail: template with grid, item page, webhook route.
